messages:
devon: heads-up — saw a sharp spike in request queueing and a handful of 503s from eu-west-1 around 10:11 UTC. latency shot up ~3x for a 3min window. :frowning:
jia: noticed that too, looks tied to a couple of model loads at once + spot pool reclaiming. warm instances weren't available so spinup latency cascaded.
samir: can you paste the timeline? was the autoscaler blocked or just slow to react?
devon: timeline — incoming QPS +80% at 10:10, admission queue depth climbed, autoscaler requested more instances at 10:11 but pods were Pending until 10:14 (image pull + model load). some requests timed out. infra-bot: incident-note created #INC-2025-07-euw1-surge
anna: sounds like two failure modes: scale-up latency for model weights + insufficient headroom. we should avoid the simultaneous weight loads by staggering or keeping preloaded burners.
jia: proposal: implement ramped provisioning window and small reserved headroom per region for bursts (e.g., keep 3% capacity for spare). also add a short admission holdback that returns 429 with Retry-After for sudden blasts instead of blocking internal queue.
samir: +1. I'd prefer a rate-limit-by-capacity approach (tokens per-GPU). admission policy example I sketched:```yamladmission:
  mode: capacity-aware
  token_bucket:
    tokens_per_gpu: 1000
    refill_ms: 1000
  fallback: 429
  queue_limit: 500
  burst_headroom_percent: 3
```
leah: can we instead do request shedding at edge layer first? e.g., circuit-break to degrade noncritical routes and keep priority ones flowing.
devon: yes, route-level prioritization already exists but not enabled for some customers. we should enable priority weights for internal high-SLA routes and for embeddings flows.
anna: Also we need to reduce model load time — swap to smaller checkpoints (quantized) for fast ramp and then warm in background. that buys time for instances to come up.
jia: ops question: how do we reconcile reserved headroom with cost goals? keeping 3% in every region adds cost. maybe make headroom dynamic: only maintain headroom when predicted demand > baseline or when spot reclaim risk is high.
samir: right — dynamic headroom + predictive scheduler. simple heuristic to start: if rolling 5m growth rate > 20% then pre-provision N nodes (N = ceil(delta * safety)).
devon: for short term: change admission policy to capacity-aware token bucket + lower queue_limit to avoid long queues, enable route prioritization for eu-west-1, and pre-provision 2 nodes on a 5m surge trigger. I'll open a PR.
infra-bot: deploy-canary started for admission-policy change in eu-west-1 (canary subset=10%)
leah: add observability: expose "headroom_pct", "pending_model_loads", and "avg_spinup_ms" on console so product teams can see tradeoffs.
jia: agree. also add an alert when queue depth crosses 400 for >60s (pager to infra-oncall).
samir: one more: tune cooldown/scale-down hysteresis — aggressive scale-down caused us to lose warmed capacity last time. set scale-down cooldown min 10m for GPU pools.
devon: action items: (1) samir to PR admission token-bucket config + tests (ETA 2h). (2) devon to enable route prioritization for high-SLA flows (ETA 1h). (3) jia to prototype dynamic headroom heuristic (ETA EOD). (4) anna to research fast-quant switch strategy and costs (ETA 2d).
anna: will also draft a short customer note if we expect transient 429s during rollout.
devon: thanks — will monitor the canary and post updates. :thumbsup:
